judge_assessment.explanation: The verdict is defensible but two of the judge's ten recomputed values contradict the artifacts, and it missed a corrupted answer key. (1) The judge reports "n>12" for problem 8. The artifact says the opposite and has to: the item plants Jonah's n < 12 for "no more than 12" and the whole point is that the boundary is included. verify.json id 8 is relation "<=" with interval (-oo, 12] and the key boxes n <= 12. (2) The judge reports "length<=14" for problem 9. Width 8 with perimeter at most 46 gives 16 + 2l <= 46, so l <= 15; verify.json id 9 expects ["-oo", 15, "loopen"] and the key boxes l <= 15 and checks that an 8 by 15 rectangle has perimeter 46. The artifacts are right and the judge's summary is wrong on both. (3) More seriously, the judge scored answer_key_quality 4 on a key whose Quick Answers row 7 literally prints "-inf, 10, <built-in function open>". The expected triple for problem 7 is ["-oo", 10, "open"], and _fmt's bare sympify resolves the string "open" to the Python builtin, which sympy.latex typesets as \mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}}. I reproduced it exactly. This is the mechanism the brief records for curr-184, reached through number-line endpoint words instead of interval words. (4) Problem 8 also asks for a one-sentence explanation and carries no manual entry, though problem 10 is correctly flagged.

strengths_to_preserve: The verification checks solution SETS, not boundary numbers: every item is a {"type": "inequality"} entry carrying the interval and its endpoint state (hiopen/loopen/open), so an answer of t <= 10 where t < 10 is correct would have failed the gate. That is what makes the strict-versus-inclusive distinction this sheet teaches actually enforceable.

The phrase-to-symbol table sits in the directions block with a third column asking "Is the boundary allowed?", so the reference the student needs is on the same page as the work and is organised around the decision rather than the vocabulary.

Problem 6 refuses to stop at the algebra: after b <= 43 the key insists the answer to the question asked is "at most 43 boxes", and the check 165 + 45(43) = 2100 lands exactly on the limit so the boundary case is real rather than decorative.

The key volunteers context restrictions the algebra does not supply — 0 <= p <= 14 for passengers on problem 2, 0 < l <= 15 for a length on problem 9 — while still telling the grader to accept the bare inequality.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt calls bare sympy.sympify on every string expected and its guard catches only SympifyError; a string that sympify RESOLVES to a non-mathematical Python object is typeset into the delivered answer key. The author's endpoint marker "open" is the Python builtin open.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers row 7 prints "-inf, 10, <built-in function open>" (pdftotext renders the angle brackets as inverted marks).
Reproduced directly: sympy.sympify('open') returns <built-in function open> and sympy.latex of it is \mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}}.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py lines 57-61 catch only SympifyError, SyntaxError, TypeError and ValueError — a successful resolution is never inspected.
The sibling markers "hiopen" and "loopen" survive only because no builtin has those names; print, eval, exec and __import__ leak the same way.

root_causes.description: final_response.md describes the three documents in prose but never names or links a single file, so the reader cannot map "the answer key" to a filename. Four other cases in this same run print the ws_/ak_/ss_ basenames.
evidence: final_response.md opens "Three PDFs are ready: the student worksheet, a full step-by-step answer key, and a two-page study guide" and contains no .pdf filename anywhere.
curr-190, curr-196, curr-197 and curr-198 in the same run each name all three files (e.g. ws_proportion_curr190.pdf).

root_causes.description: Problem 8's required explanation is unflagged while problem 10's is flagged, so the manual-item count is set by author attention rather than by a rule.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 8: "Explain in one sentence what is wrong with his symbol, write the correct inequality, and graph it."
verify.json id 8 is a single inequality entry; id 10 is correctly {"type": "manual"}.
answer_key.pdf problem 8 does print "Full credit on the sentence" criteria, so the grading guidance exists and only the declaration is missing.

improvements.title: Reject non-mathematical sympify results in the Quick Answers bank
improvements.proposed_change: Replace the bare sympy.sympify call in render_quick_answers._fmt with verify.py's sandboxed safe_parse, and add a positive type check on the result: unless it is a sympy.Basic (and not a Python callable or module), fall back to typesetting the ORIGINAL string as escaped text (\texttt{open}) rather than the resolved object's repr. The current guard catches only parse FAILURES, so every success is trusted, including successes that return a builtin.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py rendering an expected list ["-oo", 10, "open"] plus entries using "print", "eval", "exec" and "__import__": assert the bank contains none of "built-in function", "<built-in" or "function print", and that the endpoint word survives as readable text. Every assertion fails against today's renderer, which is what produced this task's key.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes a class of defect that silently corrupts a delivered answer key while every gate reports green; two confirmed instances already exist (curr-181 here, curr-184 in the brief) and any author using open/closed/print as a label word hits it.
improvements.risk: safe_parse is stricter than sympify, so some expecteds that render today would drop to the text fallback; the fallback must therefore be readable text, not the em dash, or this fix would create the very ambiguity the relation fix is removing.

improvements.title: Fail the build when a problem stem asks for reasoning and its verify entry is machine-only
improvements.proposed_change: Add a delivery-blocking lint that pairs the worksheet source with the verify JSON: scan each \problem block for an open-response demand ("explain", "say why", "say how you decided", "in one sentence", "what went wrong", "find her mistake", "describe", "sketch", "plot", "graph it") and fail the build when that problem id carries no {"type": "manual"} entry. SKILL.md should state the rule positively: a problem that asks for a value AND a sentence gets TWO verify entries, the machine one for the value and a manual one carrying the full-credit criteria, exactly as this run already does elsewhere.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture pair under tests/fixtures: a worksheet .tex whose problem 3 stem ends "Explain in one sentence why ..." beside a verify.json whose id 3 holds only an eval entry. tests/check_prose_consistency.py must exit non-zero naming problem 3; adding {"id": 3, "type": "manual", "desc": ...} makes it exit 0. The test fails today because no checker reads the stem for open-response prose.
improvements.expected_impact: The gate chain's manual-flag count starts telling the truth, so a grader is told which written answers nobody machine-checked instead of reading "nothing is flagged for manual review" under a sheet full of explanation prompts. On curr-181 problem 8's explanation joins problem 10 as a declared manual item, matching the full-credit criteria the key already prints for it.
improvements.risk: Keyword matching will flag stems whose imperative is decorative ("show your work"), so the lint needs a curated phrase list and an explicit per-problem opt-out, or authors will start declaring hollow manual entries to silence it.

improvements.title: Name every produced PDF by filename in final_response.md
improvements.proposed_change: Make the delivery step enumerate the three artifacts by their actual basenames (ws_*.pdf, ak_*.pdf, ss_*.pdf) with a one-line description each, and add a delivery check that reads the PDF names out of gate_log.txt's "PDFs" block and fails if any is absent from final_response.md. SKILL.md should show the required shape rather than leaving the format to the author.
improvements.regression_test: New test: given a gate_log.txt listing ws_x.pdf, ak_x.pdf and ss_x.pdf and a final_response.md that only says "Three PDFs are ready", the checker exits non-zero naming the three missing basenames; adding the names makes it exit 0. Running it on this task's final_response.md fails today.
improvements.expected_impact: A recipient can tell which file is the key and which is the study guide without opening all three, and the delivery message stops depending on author habit — four cases in this run name the files and two do not.
improvements.risk: Almost none. The only care needed is that the checker reads the built filenames from the log rather than assuming a naming convention, or renamed artifacts would produce spurious failures.

case_summary: A genuinely strong verbal-constraint inequality set: the boundary decision is made the assessed object, every item is verified as a solution SET with its endpoint state rather than as a boundary number, and problems 6, 7 and 10 push past the algebra into whole-number interpretation, the negative-division flip and reverse modelling. I checked all ten translations independently and the artifacts are correct throughout — including problems 8 (n <= 12) and 9 (l <= 15), where the judge's own summary reports the wrong values. The delivered answer key is nevertheless corrupted: Quick Answers row 7 prints "-inf, 10, <built-in function open>" because the endpoint marker "open" sympifies to the Python builtin. final_response.md also never names a file, and problem 8's required sentence is not declared manual although problem 10's is.
